propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Deus, qui in tuae caritatis exemplum ad fidelium redemptionem sanctum Petrum
Ecclesiam tuam nova prole fecundare divinitus docuisti: ipsius nobis
intercessione concede; a peccati servitute solutis, in caelesti patria
perpetua libertate gaudere: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

translations.text: O God, Who, as a token of Thy loving-kindness, didst inspire holy Peter to enrich Thy Church with a new progeny devoted to the redemption of the faithful, grant that, being delivered through his intercession from the servitude of sin, we may know the joys of eternal freedom in heaven, our native land. Who livest.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Laudis tibi, Domine, hostias immolamus in tuorum commemoratione Sanctorum:
quibus nos et praesentibus exui malis confidimus, et futuris. Per Dominum
nostrum Jesum Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A pre-1955 lay hand missal, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its rubrics, its seasonal second and third orations, its Holy Week and its sanctoral are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

The 1962 target prints the exact Mass-XIII Secret as proper to Peter Nolasco; the 1861 day appoints another Common, but the historical English body itself is an exact target antecedent. The 1962 target body is word-for-word identical to the name-free Cummiskey Mass-XIII formula. This binding is by exact text identity only and does not claim that Cummiskey appointed that Common to Peter Nolasco.
